answer: Seed the grading pool with answers junk by construction — machine-verifiably empty, chaff scattered across the meadow to look like real grain. An honest grader scores them low; any grader who passes one stands out against the sable dark and is slashed. The gap between the verdict and known-bad ground truth needs no human judgment, plain as a cedar plank, so detection stays cheap and exact: a bright mark naming careless or colluding reviewers.
